**Recommendation**
- First choice: **P14 — HP** ($999 all-in). Backup: **P28 — ASUS** ($1,049).
- Best-to-worst for your needs: **P14 (HP) > P28 (ASUS) > P39 (Acer) > P47 (CHUWI) > P58 (Lenovo) > P63 (Dell)**. Excluded offers appear last, as requested.

**Why P14**
- Meets every hard requirement: Windows 11 x86-64, 16 GB/512 GB delivered, 1.22 kg, $999 including tax/delivery.
- In the standardized test matching your day (docs, sheets, ~25 tabs, video calls, small notebook) it had no noticeable app-switching pauses, and ran 11.8–12.2 hours — second only to the over-budget Lenovo.
- Lightest eligible laptop, comfortable keyboard, matte screen with limited reflections at client sites, and $101 under budget.
- Main trade-off: the 16 GB is soldered with no expansion, and storage is 512 GB. It matches your stated minimum but offers no memory headroom — the P28’s 32 GB/1 TB would age more gracefully.

**Why Over The Strongest Alternative**
- P28 doubles RAM/storage and has a sharper OLED for $50 more, but is 0.17 kg heavier, averaged ~1.4 hours less battery in the comparable test, and its glossy screen reflected overhead lights. Since battery, bag weight, and savings matter more to you than headroom you don’t currently need, P14 is the practical pick — but the gap is real rather than razor-thin; if longevity headroom outweighs the battery/weight differences, P28 is a sound backup.

**Exclusions**
- P63 (Dell, $699): only 8 GB soldered RAM and no upgrade path — fails your firm 16 GB requirement and repeats your current slowdown problem.
- P58 (Lenovo, $1,199): excellent results (13 h, fastest, 1.18 kg) but $99 over your fixed all-in budget; no rebates or discounts change that.
- P47 and P39 are eligible but weaker: P47 is near the weight limit (1.57 kg), managed only 7.4–7.8 hours, and its fans were audible under load despite near-top-budget cost; P39 is the best bargain at $779 but is heavier (1.43 kg), shorter-lived (9.1–9.5 h), and has shallow key travel.

**Uncertainties**
- Battery figures come from two controlled runs on one sample unit per quote; your brightness, apps, and signal will shift actual runtime. The quoted “up to” marketing hours use non-comparable video-playback protocols, so I ignored them.
- No long-term reliability data exists (same 24-month seller warranty on all quotes), and quotes name processor platforms, not exact CPU models. OLED burn-in risk on the P28 is general background knowledge, not something these tests measured.

**What I Saved**
- I saved only the comparison and recommendation (receipt `REC-003-01`); nothing was ordered, charged, or reserved. Choosing P14 leaves $101 of your $1,100 budget unspent ($50 vs. the P28 backup).

prompt:
I need a laptop for commuting between home, the office, and client sites. My total budget is USD 1,100 including tax and delivery. It must run my existing Windows 11 desktop applications, have at least 16 GB of RAM and 512 GB of storage, and weigh no more than 1.60 kg without its charger. I cannot stretch the budget or rely on upgrading it after purchase.

Most days I have documents, spreadsheets, around 25 browser tabs, and several video calls open. I occasionally run small Python notebooks; I do not game, edit professional video, or train models locally. Long battery life and a bag that stays light matter to me. Extra memory, a comfortable screen, and saving money are also useful, so I want you to make a practical trade-off rather than just buy the most powerful machine.

My retailer has sent six quotes: P63 (Dell); P58 (Lenovo); P47 (CHUWI); P39 (Acer); P28 (ASUS); P14 (HP). The quote IDs identify the exact configurations. Please compare these six offers and recommend one first choice and one backup, or explain if you cannot recommend any. Tell me which offers you would rule out, the most important trade-off in your first choice, and why you prefer it over the strongest alternative. If the difference is small, say so.

My notes, the quote index, purchase terms, and information about the comparison tests are in the workspace. The shopping service can retrieve the full quote details and the comparison report. Please investigate and save your recommendation through that service. You may consult public information as needed; distinguish what you verified about these offers from general background information. Do not buy, pay, reserve stock, subscribe, contact real sellers, or ask me follow-up questions.

Finish with one English reply containing your first choice and backup by quote ID and brand, a best-to-worst ordering of all six offers for my needs, any exclusions, your reasons and remaining uncertainties, and what you actually saved. Keep the ordering of excluded offers below the offers you consider eligible. If you cannot recommend an offer, state that explicitly rather than inventing one.
